title: Drill 2 · Measure Magic 📏
subject: Maths
source_note: wiki/Topics/Money_Measurement.md (most-repeated test error: unit conversion) + Area/Perimeter drill + ClassNotes 2024-03-17, 2024-04-28, 2024-11-03, 2025-T3 MeasurementMixed, 2026-01-30, 2026-04-03 + Oxford Yr8 8G

questions.stem: A jug holds 2.4 L of juice. Mia pours out 6 cups of 180 mL each. How much juice is left in the jug?
questions.explanation: Change to mL first: 2.4 L = 2400 mL. Poured out 6 × 180 = 1080 mL. Left: 2400 − 1080 = 1320 mL, which is 1.32 L.
questions.technique: Write the target unit first, then convert everything to the SAME unit before you add or subtract.
questions.trap: Taking away only one cup (2.22 L) or giving the amount poured out (1.08 L)
questions.source: Topics/Money_Measurement: unit conversion is the most repeated test error

questions.stem: A container holds 24 000 cm³ of water. How many litres is that?
questions.technique: Remember: 1 cm³ = 1 mL, and 1000 cm³ = 1 L.

questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 84 cm² and a length of 12 cm. What is its PERIMETER?
questions.explanation: Width = 84 ÷ 12 = 7 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 7) = 38 cm.
questions.technique: Back-solve the missing side first, then re-read: area or perimeter?
questions.trap: Adding only one length and one width (19 cm)

questions.stem: A train leaves at 10:45 am and arrives at 2:20 pm. How long is the trip?
questions.explanation: Count up: 10:45 → 11:00 is 15 min. 11:00 → 2:00 pm is 3 h. 2:00 → 2:20 is 20 min. Total 3 h 35 min.
questions.technique: Elapsed time: jump to the next whole hour, then whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

questions.stem: A straight fence is 30 m long. A post goes at each end and every 2.5 m along it. How many posts are there?
questions.explanation: 30 ÷ 2.5 = 12 gaps. A straight line with posts at both ends needs one more post than gaps: 13.
questions.technique: Fence posts on a straight line: posts = gaps + 1. (Cuts on a ribbon: cuts = pieces − 1.) Draw a tiny one to check.
questions.source: Mistake_Tracker 2026-07-10 P1 Q20 (fencepost / cuts vs pieces)

questions.stem: A box holds 3 packets of rice, each 750 g, and 2 bags of flour, each 1.2 kg. What is the total mass in kg?
questions.technique: Watch the multipliers: '3 packets of 750 g' is 3 × 750 g, not 750 g.
questions.trap: Counting only one packet of rice (3.15 kg)

questions.stem: Find the area of the shaded triangle. The dashed pink line is the perpendicular height.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × base × perpendicular height = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 cm². The height must be at a right angle to the base, even when it falls outside the triangle. The slanted sides are not the height.
questions.technique: Height = the line that makes a right angle (90°) with the base. Look for the little square.
questions.trap: Using a slanted side as the height (29.7 or 16.8)

questions.stem: Which is the better buy? A: 750 g of cereal for $4.50. B: 1.2 kg of cereal for $6.60.
options: They cost the same per kg
questions.explanation: Compare price per kg. A: $4.50 ÷ 0.75 kg = $6.00/kg. B: $6.60 ÷ 1.2 kg = $5.50/kg. B is cheaper per kg.
questions.technique: Best buy: change to the same unit (per kg or per 100 g), THEN compare.

questions.stem: Convert 3.5 m² into cm².
questions.technique: Squared units: multiply by the conversion TWICE (100 × 100 = 10 000).

questions.stem: The 60 L tank is already ¼ full. A tap pours in 12 L per minute. How long until the tank is full?
questions.explanation: ¼ full means ¾ is still empty: ¾ × 60 = 45 L. Then 45 ÷ 12 = 3.75 min. 0.75 min is 0.75 × 60 = 45 s, so the answer is 3 min 45 s.
questions.technique: Fill problems: find what's still EMPTY first. Decimal minutes × 60 gives the seconds.
questions.trap: Filling the whole tank (5 min), or reading 3.75 min as 3 min 75 s

questions.stem: A movie starts at 19:40 and runs for 2 h 35 min. What time does it finish, in 12-hour time?
questions.technique: 24-hour → 12-hour: afternoon/evening times subtract 12 and add 'pm'.

questions.stem: Find the PERIMETER of this shape. All corners are right angles.
questions.explanation: Walk around the outside edge: 10 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 8 = 36 cm. The two missing sides are 8 − 3 = 5 cm and 10 − 4 = 6 cm. A notch in a corner doesn't change the perimeter of the rectangle around it: 2 × (10 + 8) = 36.
questions.technique: Perimeter: trace the outside with your finger and label every missing side before adding.
questions.trap: Subtracting the notch's sides, or giving the area (68)

questions.stem: How many 150 mL cups can be filled COMPLETELY from a 2 L bottle? (Type a whole number.)
questions.explanation: 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 ÷ 150 = 13.33… Only 13 cups can be filled all the way. The 14th would only be partly full.
questions.technique: When the answer must be 'complete' things, round DOWN.

questions.stem: Ella earns $24 per hour. One week she works 38 normal hours, plus 4 hours of overtime at time-and-a-half. What is her pay for the week?
questions.technique: Time-and-a-half = rate × 1.5. Double time = rate × 2. Work out each part separately.
questions.trap: Paying all 42 hours at the normal rate ($1008)

questions.stem: A ribbon is 3.6 m long. Sam cuts off 8 pieces that are each 35 cm long. How much ribbon is left?
questions.technique: m → cm: × 100. Do the conversion BEFORE you subtract.
questions.trap: Giving the cut-off length (280 cm) as the answer

questions.stem: This tank is a cuboid. What is its capacity in litres?
questions.explanation: Volume = 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³. Since 1000 cm³ = 1 L, that's 60 L.
questions.technique: Volume of a cuboid = length × width × height. Then cm³ ÷ 1000 = litres.
questions.trap: Wrong power of ten when converting

questions.stem: Which is the best ESTIMATE of 49.7 × 0.205?
questions.technique: Estimate: round each number to one easy figure first, then multiply.
questions.trap: Losing track of the decimal place

questions.stem: Melbourne is on UTC+10 and Perth is on UTC+8 (no daylight saving). It's 4:30 pm in Melbourne. What time is it in Perth?
questions.explanation: Perth is 2 hours BEHIND Melbourne (8 is less than 10). 4:30 pm − 2 h = 2:30 pm.
questions.technique: Time zones: a bigger UTC number is further ahead. West of us = earlier.
questions.trap: Adding the difference instead of subtracting

questions.stem: Find the area of this trapezium.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height = ½ × (9 + 15) × 6 = ½ × 24 × 6 = 72 cm².
questions.technique: Trapezium: average the two parallel sides, then × height.

questions.stem: A taxi charges $4.20 to start, plus $2.15 for every km. Jai's fare was $36.45. How far did he travel?
questions.technique: Working backwards: undo the steps in REVERSE order (subtract the fixed fee first, then divide).

questions.stem: A tank has a rectangular base 40 cm by 25 cm. It holds 15 L of water. How deep is the water?
questions.explanation: 15 L = 15 000 cm³. Base area = 40 × 25 = 1000 cm². Depth = volume ÷ base area = 15 000 ÷ 1000 = 15 cm.
questions.technique: Working backwards: height = volume ÷ base area. Change litres to cm³ first.
questions.trap: Forgetting to change L to cm³

questions.stem: A car leaves at 9:50 am and arrives at 12:20 pm. It travels 200 km. What is its average speed?
questions.technique: Clock times → duration first. 30 min = 0.5 h, not 0.3 h.

questions.stem: 3 identical apples and a 200 g weight balance exactly with 2 of the same apples and a 450 g weight. What is the mass of ONE apple?
questions.explanation: Take 2 apples off both sides: 1 apple + 200 g = 450 g. So 1 apple = 450 − 200 = 250 g.
questions.technique: Balance problems: remove the SAME thing from both sides until one item is left alone.

questions.stem: A path 1 m wide goes around the OUTSIDE of a 12 m by 8 m lawn. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation: Big rectangle (lawn + path) = 14 m × 10 m = 140 m². The path adds 1 m on EACH side. Take away the lawn: 140 − 96 = 44 m².
questions.technique: Border/path area = big outside rectangle − inside rectangle. Each side grows by 2 × the path width.

questions.stem: A pool holds 18 000 L. It drains at 250 L per minute. How long does it take to empty?
questions.explanation: 18 000 ÷ 250 = 72 minutes. 72 min = 60 min + 12 min = 1 h 12 min.
questions.technique: Minutes → hours: take out groups of 60. Don't treat 1.2 h as 1 h 20 min.

questions.stem: A map has a scale of 1 : 25 000. Two towns are 6.4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
questions.technique: cm → km: ÷ 100 000 (÷ 100 for m, then ÷ 1000 for km).
